market_question: US x Iran permanent peace deal by June 30, 2026?
reasoning: US-Iran permanent peace deal by mid-2026 is extremely unlikely given ongoing hostility, no active negotiations, and the profound political changes required on both sides. The market-implied 26.5% probability is far too high.
evidence_points: No formal US-Iran peace process exists; maximum pressure and sanctions remain in place.
A permanent treaty would require mutual recognition, security guarantees, and reversal of decades of enmity — none is even being discussed.
Historical precedent: since the 1979 revolution, no permanent peace accord has been signed; even the JCPOA was a nuclear deal, not a peace treaty.
sources_consulted: Council on Foreign Relations backgrounders on US-Iran relations
Recent White House statements on Iran policy
News reports on Iran nuclear enrichment and US sanctions
